newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London buoyed by firm dollar.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London buoyed by firm dollar.

text.p: Japanese shares trading in London powered ahead on Monday as a firm dollar/yen exchange rate fuelled further gains for exporters, dealers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average looked poised to test its 1997 high of 20,681, they said, and could target 21,000.
"We're very much firmer," one London dealer said.

"We had a good move in Tokyo on the back of a firm dollar, which averaged about 117.2 yen overnight. Now it's just below 118 and people are chasing after the exporters, there's a lot of follow through buying."
Dealers said Sony Corp, Bridgestone Corp and Fujitsu Ltd were looking particularly well bid.
"There's every chance the Nikkei will have a good run at the year high of 20,681, with the currency where it is, and almost certainly break through," a dealer said.

"We've tried maybe three or four times in the last few months to break through that level and never quite managed it. But I think tonight we could well see the market go through that level. The next stopping point would be 21,000."
The dollar was trading at 117.65/70 yen by 1410 GMT. The Nikkei 50 index in London was at 1,711.51 points, up 6.46 points or 0.39 percent from Friday's London close.
